title: Head lice: checking and treating without stigma
intro: Head lice are small insects living on scalp hair. They spread mainly through head-to-head contact and are not a sign of poor cleanliness. Itching may occur, but checking is needed because not every itchy scalp has lice.

sections.heading: Understanding the problem
paragraphs: Finding a living louse confirms active infestation more reliably than old egg cases alone. Use a fine detection comb with good lighting; ask for help if the scalp is sore or the finding is uncertain.

sections.heading: Assessment and tests
paragraphs: Check close household contacts and treat active cases together according to advice. Discuss the person’s age, pregnancy, allergies and prior treatment before selecting a product; local resistance can affect effectiveness. Bring your medicine list and previous results; ask which findings would change the plan.

sections.heading: Treatment choices
paragraphs: Wet-combing regimens or suitable lice treatments are options. Follow the complete schedule and product-specific repeat instructions precisely. Do not combine products indiscriminately or use kerosene, insect sprays or animal treatments. Agree how benefit and adverse effects will be checked before changing treatment.

sections.heading: Everyday care
paragraphs: Clean combs and avoid sharing hair-contact items during treatment. Extensive house fumigation or treating pets is unnecessary. Tell relevant close contacts discreetly and follow local school guidance without blaming a child. Choose a routine you can maintain, and discuss barriers such as cost, work or language.

sections.heading: Follow-up and warning signs
paragraphs: Recheck for living lice after treatment. Persistent infestation may reflect incomplete use, reinfection or resistance rather than poor hygiene. Seek advice for infected scratch wounds, severe irritation or repeated treatment failure.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira finds only empty old egg cases after treatment. She checks carefully for living lice before repeating chemicals unnecessarily.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben coordinates checks in the household and follows the product’s repeat schedule instead of using several different treatments on the same evening.
